key_insight: Full hydrogenation converts metallic irida-graphene into predicted irida-graphane, an indirect wide-band-gap semiconductor with a 6.0 eV HSE06 gap.
engineering_relevance: Predicted visible transparency and strong deep-ultraviolet absorption make irida-graphane a candidate for UV optoelectronics and transparent coatings.
method: PBE and HSE06 density functional theory calculations
Phonon analysis and ab initio molecular dynamics
Structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical characterization
evidence_signal: Calculations show no imaginary phonon frequencies, structural integrity in AIMD up to 2000 K, visible reflectivity below 0.3%, and deep-UV absorption of 10^5–10^6 cm⁻¹.
watch_item: These computational predictions require experimental synthesis and validation; exothermic hydrogenation alone does not establish a practical fabrication route.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
